# `kernel/FxBus.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/FxBus.js`

FxBus.js — the OS "FX Bridge". A normalized pipeline that lets apps (and the OS itself) publish a lightweight "vibe" — a dominant accent color, optional palette, an energy level, and an optional beat/mood — which the desktop reacts to (ambient tint/pulse, accent glow) and which external sinks (WLED / Home Assistant / Hue via a relay) can later subscribe to. Producers: - Explicit: an app calls `syscalls.fx.publish(frame)` (capability `fx.emit`). Sandboxed iframe guests call `window.os.fx.publish(frame)`, routed over the existing postMessage RPC bridge. - Automatic: `startAutoSample()` samples a provided surface (canvas/img/video) and extracts the dominant color, so an app can drive effects with no code. Consumers subscribe to the kernel event `os:fx-frame`. The built-in consumer is AmbientEngine.fxTint(); more sinks can be added without touching producers. Frames are normalized and rate-limited (coalesced to ~one emit per minInterval) so a chatty producer cannot flood the desktop or thrash the compositor.

### `class FxBus`

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor(kernel)` |  |
| `mount` | `mount()` | Subscribe the built-in desktop sink (ambient tint). Safe to call once. |
| `unmount` | `unmount()` |  |
| `publish` | `publish(appId, frame)` | Publish an FX frame from `appId` (may be null for OS/anonymous sources). |
| `latest` | `latest(appId)` | Last frame for an app, or the last emitted frame overall when appId omitted. |
| `onFrame` | `onFrame(cb)` | Subscribe to emitted frames. Returns an unsubscribe fn. |
| `_schedule` | `_schedule(frame)` |  |
| `_emit` | `_emit(frame, now)` |  |
| `setSurfaceProvider` | `setSurfaceProvider(fn)` | Set a provider that returns the surface to sample — an HTMLCanvasElement, <img>, <video>, or null. The shell can point this at the focused app's canvas. (Cross-origin / sandboxed guest canvases are unreadable by design; those guests publish explicitly instead.) |
| `startAutoSample` | `startAutoSample(appId = null, intervalMs = 250)` | Begin sampling the provider surface every `intervalMs` and publishing its vibe. |
| `stopAutoSample` | `stopAutoSample()` |  |
| `extractVibe` | `extractVibe(source, opts = {})` | Extract a vibe (dominant accent + small palette + energy) from a drawable source. Returns null on failure (e.g. a cross-origin-tainted canvas). |

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
